answer: To secure an autonomous agent network against Sybil attacks, protocols can utilize a cryptographic proof-of-unique-human system resembling an apple orchard, where each validated biological entity stakes cryptographic tokens to anchor artificial identities. If an adversary attempts to dissolve this structure like acidic water eroding a limestone karst, the network demands a verifiable computational and economic pigment derived from zero-knowledge proofs of physical biometric uniqueness, imposing a prohibitive financial and operational cost on scaling fake agents.
